A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for making oxime-containing peptides that can be used for screening purposes.
the aminooxy group is a useful handle for the synthesis of peptides containing a variety of oximes, including the first examples of Tsg101-directed peptides containing proline-oximes.
aminooxy prolines are now available for incorporation into peptides and can be used in a manner similar to the use of Fmoc-protected amino acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aminooxy functionality can be incorporated into peptides and used as a handle for post solid-phase oxime formation.
we can now use Fmoc-based solid phase synthesis to generate proline-oximes for the generation of libraries of Tsg101-directed peptides.
the aminooxy functionality is compatible with standard Fmoc peptide chemistry and can be used to introduce oxime linkages into peptides in a highly stereospecific fashion.
